target_customer: Small shop owners acting as payment agents and, later, Indonesian and Singapore small businesses buying payments, cash accounts, cards and lending
problem: Unbanked and underbanked Indonesians cannot easily pay bills or access financial services, and small businesses lack modern finance tools.
business_model: Agent network taking a commission on bill payments, later B2B payments, neobank and lending revenue
product_category: Fintech, agent banking and B2B payments

founders.name: Hendra Kwik
founders.background_notes: YC page says the founders are ex Amazon, Grab, Quora and Traveloka without assigning employers to individuals; education not given.

founders.name: Jefriyanto
founders.background_notes: Named on YC page; no individual background found.

founders.name: Ricky Winata
founders.background_notes: Named on YC page; no individual background found.

competitors.name: Kudo (Grab)
competitors.what: Agent based commerce and payments platform for offline shops, acquired by Grab

technical_complexity.rationale: Agent app, wallet balances and bank integrations with KYC are standard fintech engineering with regulatory and partner complexity.

defensibility.rationale: A large agent network and later licenses are hard to replicate, though bill payment itself was commoditized at founding.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Grab bought Kudo in Feb 2017 and offered warung services; no source shows Grab absorbing Payfazz, which reached Series C in 2022.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in August 2017 described unbanked customers paying bills in cash through agents, with agents expected to earn about $100 to $200 a month, indicating demand for cash-to-digital payment access.

identity.logo: new logo and colours introduced in 2022 rebrand
identity.voice_and_tone: progressive, dynamic, inclusive per company statement

rebrands.why: Payfazz invested $30M in Xfers to form a combined group; Xfers later became Fazz Business
Company announced a new logo, colours, tagline and website on 29 August 2022 per its site

brand_strength.rationale: Search found company announcements about the rebrand but no independent press about the brand, merch or community.

pivots.to: Multi-country B2B finance group with Xfers (Fazz)
pivots.why: Payfazz invested $30M in Xfers to form Fazz Financial Group for Indonesia and Singapore.

outcome_analysis: Payfazz built an agent network in Indonesia, raised a $53M Series B in 2020 and merged with Xfers in 2021 to form Fazz, then announced a $100M Series C in 2022 including debt per one aggregator. It reports multi-billion dollar annualized volume on its own site. A reported staff reduction shows later pressure, but the company remains active.
notes: Website fazzfinancial.com redirects to fazz.com, whose fetch was not retained. No rounds found before Series B; YC page says over $74M raised, which conflicts with $53M plus $100M, so totals are unreconciled. Series C lead is Tiger Global per Crowdfund Insider; AVCJ lists participants; one aggregator says $75M equity plus $25M Lendable debt, unverified. A layoff report (DailySocial, year unconfirmed, up to 15 percent per social claims) is unverified. A $13M 2026 strategic investment on an aggregator is unverified.
